_comment: Provenance for the BURN loop set. Every delivered loop in loops/ is built
from one of these Higgsfield generations by tools/build_loops.sh.
All were generated with Seedance 2.0, 16:9, 720p, std mode, 10s requested
(the model returns 241 frames = 10.041667s at 24fps), using the SAME image
as both start_image and end_image so the model is obliged to return to its
origin. That is the core loop technique - see CONCEPT_BURN_10S_LOOP.md 5.1.
Delivered length is 9.541667s (229 frames), not 10.000s: the 0.5s overlap
blend is subtracted from the source and nothing is retimed to make it back
up. See the duration note in build_loops.sh.

clips.title: Last Road (DELIVERED)
clips.note: The delivered loop. Seedance 2.0, 10s, 16:9, 1080p, std, silent, keyframe v12 as BOTH start_image and end_image. 90 credits. The raw render judders in its last ~2s (a 4-frame cadence from frame 190 on), so the source is trimmed to 7.875s BEFORE blending, then blended 0.5s with no retime -> 7.375s / 177 frames. Loop 1.04x, pace cv 0.055, both gates pass.

superseded.note: First take of A, from an uploaded start frame. Replaced by A_PhoenixHour, which re-staged the town closer and warmed the key. Verifies clean (1.18x) but is not delivered.

Reserve re-render, 90 credits, same keyframe, prompt rewritten to force a constant pace. It did not work: pace got worse, not better (cv 0.328 vs 0.275, ends/middle 0.82 vs 0.97 - textbook ease in/out) plus a motion spike at ~6.3s. Trimming its ease-in still failed at cv 0.310. Not used. The lesson is that prompt wording does not beat the structural pull of start=end conditioning; trimming does.
